workEn: The Secret History of the Mongols
title: 元朝秘史 §§140–143
titleEn: The Secret History of the Mongols — §§140–143: The Wrestling, and Jamuqa's Host
part: §§140–143 — The Wrestling of Büri-Bökö, and Jamuqa's Host
source: Mongγol-un niγuča tobčiyan (The Secret History of the Mongols), §§140–143, in the Ming Chinese-character phonetic transcription, as edited with a romanized reading by Shiratori Kurakichi 白鳥庫吉, 音訳蒙文元朝秘史 (Tokyo, 1943), itself based on the Ye Dehui 葉德輝 printed edition of 1905/1908; text taken from the Japanese Wikisource transcription, archived and verified against it character for character. Shiratori died in 1942, so the edition was public domain in Japan before the URAA date and was never restored in the United States. Section numbering (§) is the standard citation system. Romanization convention: Shiratori's, kept exactly as he prints it (γ, ġ, ṅ, ž, č, and the raised dot of γ̇). Translations are made fresh from the Mongolian, with the Ming interlinear Chinese glosses as the primary crib. No modern translation was consulted. langCode is null: there is no text-to-speech for Middle Mongol.
about: Four sections. §140 is the wrestling match: Chinggis sets Büri-Bökö, the realm's champion of the Jurkin, against Belgütei; Büri-Bökö gives way, Belgütei, reading a sign from the Qahan, breaks his spine, and the dying man blames his own fear of the Qahan. A short genealogy ties him to the line of Qabul Qahan. §141 lists the peoples who gather at Alqui-Bulaq, raise Jamuqa as Gur-Qan and swear by a cut stallion and mare, and tells how Qoridai carries word of their plan to Chinggis, who passes it to Wang Qan, who brings his army. §142 sets out both vanguards, the posts of scouts, the first meeting with Jamuqa's four vanguard leaders, and the withdrawal to camp. §143 is the battle at Köiten, where the two weather-workers raise a storm that turns on themselves. Several clauses rest on the Ming glosses alone — the kinship sentence in §140, the details of the bout, and the verb ile- — and the English is a first drafting.
draftNote: The Mongol readings follow Shiratori throughout; the English is a first drafting.

sentences.l: Čiṅgis Qaγan, one day: "Büri-Bökö, Belgütei, the two (acc.) — let them be made to wrestle," said.
sentences.i: One day Chinggis Qahan said, "Let Büri-Bökö and Belgütei be set to wrestle."
sentences.n: abalduγ̇uluja is a verb with its parts stacked: a stem, the reciprocal -ldu- 'with one another', the causative -γ̇ul- 'make', and the hortative -ja 'let …': 'let the two be made to grapple'; the Ming glosses it 敎断搏咱. The stem abal- is the one in abaldurun 'when grappling' in earlier parts, itself inferred from the Ming 搏 'grapple', so it is still uncertain. qojar-i 'the two' takes the accusative -i (Ming 兩箇 行). Shiratori's quotation mark opens in the middle of the sentence, on Büri-Bökö.

sentences.i: Büri-Bökö was among the Jurkin.
sentences.n: Žürkin-dür is the clan name with the dative-locative -dür (Ming 行). Earlier it meant 'against the Jurkin'; here it is 'among, in' — the case is wide and the sense is left to the verb. büleġe is 'there was, used to be'; Mongol supplies no copula, so the English 'was' is all the verb there is.

sentences.i: Büri-Bökö seized Belgütei with one hand, tripped him (?) with one foot, and threw him down,
sentences.n: A converb chain, broken after unaγ̇ažu 'causing to fall'. -jar / -jer is the instrumental 'with' (the Ming writes 用 'using'): γar-jar 'with the hand', köl-jer 'with the foot'; the bracketed (i) is Shiratori's. öröġele (一隻) is 'one of a pair', said twice: 'one hand … one foot'. töidčü is doubtful: I know no stem töid-, and the Ming 揆着 is obscure; 'tripping, hooking' is a guess from the wrestling.

sentences.i: and kept him pressed down, not letting him stir.
sentences.n: ülü 'not' negates the converb that follows: ülü ködölgen 'not making (him) move'. ködölgen (敎動) is ködöl- 'move' with a causative and the converb -n; I take the causative from the Ming 敎 and the exact ending is uncertain. daruqu is dara- 'press down' with the participle -qu, and with büleġe it gives 'was pressing, kept pressing'. The tense may be habitual ('used to hold him so'); I read it as the bout.

sentences.l: There Belgütei, Büri-Bökö the two (acc.) was-made-to-wrestle.
sentences.i: So there Belgütei and Büri-Bökö were set to wrestle.
sentences.n: tende is 'there' (Ming 那裏). abalduγ̇ulba is the verb of Chinggis's order now in the past, -ba (敎厮搏了 'made them grapple'); the one who makes them is not named (so the English is passive, not 'he had them wrestle'), and the two are the accusative object, qojar-i. The chronicle jumps back here: the bout is the order carried out.

sentences.i: Büri-Bökö, a man who could not be beaten, went down and gave way.
sentences.n: ülü ilaγdaqu küġün is 'a man not to be overcome': ilaγ- 'overcome' (inferred from the Ming 可勝 'able to win') + the passive -da- + the participle -qu. unažu ögbe (倒着 與了) is 'falling, gave'; ög- 'give' after a converb can be a helper verb. Who falls is not said. I read that Büri-Bökö let himself go down — his own words below say he held back from the fall — but 'Belgütei fell' is the other reading. Uncertain.

The text does not say what the bitten lip signals; the next unit shows Belgütei understood it.

sentences.i: "Belgütei could not have beaten me.
sentences.n: Belgütei-je, like Žürukin-e in §136, is a dative-type ending naming the doer of a passive: 'by Belgütei' (the Ming writes 行). I have not met -je elsewhere, so its form is uncertain. ülü ilaγdaqu is the same 'not to be overcome' as above; bi büleġe is 'I was'. The quotation opens on the first word as Shiratori prints it.

sentences.i: Afraid of the Qahan, I used craft, I hesitated over the fall — and so I have brought this on my own life."
sentences.n: A hard sentence, and the Ming is a string of single glosses: 阿余周 'fearing', 使智量 'using wit', 倒的 'falling', 猶豫的 'hesitating', 上頭 'on account of'. I read him saying that fear of the Qahan made him play a craftily slack part in the fall, and so he brought death on himself; that reading is uncertain. -(n)ača is the ablative 'from'; amin-dur(i)-jan is 'to his own life' (dative-locative + the reflexive -jan, the (i) Shiratori's); kürtebe (敎到了) 'caused to reach', 'brought to'. arγadan, from arγa 'means, craft', is read from the Ming. The closing quotation mark follows bi.

sentences.n: Another converb chain, quγuru tataγ̇ad čirčü oγ̇orkižu — 'snapping, having pulled, dragging, going' — closed by jorčiba 'went'. His spine has already been broken in the Ming's telling above, so I take this as the dragging-off of the body; the stems quγuru (折折), oγ̇orkižu (去着) and jorčiba are read from the Ming, and oγ̇orki- I cannot analyse at all.

sentences.l: Qabul Qān's seven sons' elder-brother Ökin-Barqaγ there was;
sentences.i: The eldest of Qabul Qahan's seven sons was Ökin-Barqaq;
sentences.n: A genealogy begins, in the usual order: possessor before possessed. Qān-u is 'of the Qan' (printed Qān; the English keeps Qahan for Qabul, as in earlier parts), köġüd-ün is köġün 'son' + the plural -d + the genitive -ün: 'of the sons'. aqa is 'elder brother' (Ming 兄長), so doloγ̇an köġüd-ün aqa reads 'the eldest of the seven sons'. The name Ökin-Barqaγ (斡勤-巴舌兒中合黑) is Shiratori's spelling.

sentences.l: Barilduγ̇a: Bartan-Baγ̇atur's son-from passing-beyond, Barqaγ's bold sons-to companion, on-account,
sentences.i: Adjoining, passing beyond the son of Bartan-Ba'atur, a companion to the bold sons of Barqaq, and on that account
sentences.n: A kinship sentence, and uncertain throughout. barilduγ̇a (相挨) is 'adjoining, abutting' — bari- 'take hold of' with the reciprocal -ldu- and an ending I cannot name — and alus (越過) is 'passing beyond'; together they seem to say how one line is joined to another; I do not say which. nököčekün (作伴的) is 'a companion', and bolun (上頭) 'on that account' ties the sentence to the one that follows. omoγtan (勇 有的) is omoγ 'pride, daring' + the possessive plural -tan, 'those having daring'. I give the words, not a certain sense.

morph.gloss: forehead, brow; the vanguard (Ming 頭哨 'lead scouts') [頭哨]

sentences.l: These vanguard-from forward again scouts when-sending;
sentences.i: From these vanguards, further forward, when they sent out scouts again;
sentences.n: ede is 'these' (Ming 這(的每)); maṅlan-ača is 'from the vanguards' (頭哨處), the ablative -ača. uruγši (向前) 'forward' and basa (再) 'again'. qaraγ̇ul is 'scout, watch' (哨望), and ilerün (敎去時) is ile- 'send' with the converb of time -rün: 'when sending'. Shiratori's semicolon closes the clause.

sentences.t: Enegen, Küiletü-de nigen saγ̇urin Qaraγ̇ul talbiba.

morph.gloss: Enegen, a place name (Ming (地名)) [(地名)]
a place for sitting, a post, a station (from saγ̇u- 'sit'; read from the Ming 坐位) [坐位]
to let go, set loose, release [放了]

sentences.l: Enegen, at-Küiletü one post scouts set.
sentences.i: At Enegen Küiletü they set one post of scouts.
sentences.n: Enegen and Küiletü-de are two place names with a comma between them (Ming (地名) and 地名(行)); I am not sure whether they are two names or one place. saγ̇urin (坐位) is 'a seat, a post', nigen saγ̇urin 'one post'; talbiba is talbi- 'let go, set down' in the past: 'set (the scouts) in place'.

sentences.t: Teġün-ü činana Čegčer-e nigen saγ̇urin qaraγ̇ul tabiγ̇ulba.

morph.gloss: that, that one; also 'he, she' (stem teġün- before case endings) [那的]
on the far side, beyond (the Ming 那邊 'that side') [那邊]
a place for sitting, a post, a station (from saγ̇u- 'sit'; read from the Ming 坐位) [坐位]
to let go, set loose, release (a spelling of talbi-) [敎放了]

sentences.l: Of-that beyond, at-Čegčer one post scouts caused-to-be-set.
sentences.i: Beyond that, at Chegcher, they had one post of scouts set.
sentences.n: činana (那邊) is 'on the farther side, beyond', and teġün-ü is 'of that', so 'beyond that'. Čegčer-e takes the dative-locative -e (Ming 行). tabiγ̇ulba (敎放了) is the same verb talbi- as above, spelled without the l and with the causative -γ̇ul-: 'caused to be set'.

sentences.t: Teġün-ü činana Čiqurqu-da nigen saγ̇urin Qaraγ̇ul tabiγ̇ulba.

morph.gloss: that, that one; also 'he, she' (stem teġün- before case endings) [那的]
on the far side, beyond (the Ming 那邊 'that side') [那邊]

words.reading: 赤中忽舌兒中忽-荅 Čiqurqu-da

morph.gloss: a place for sitting, a post, a station (from saγ̇u- 'sit'; read from the Ming 坐位) [坐位]
to let go, set loose, release (a spelling of talbi-) [敎放了]

sentences.l: Of-that beyond, at-Čiqurqu one post scouts caused-to-be-set.
sentences.i: Beyond that, at Chiqurqu, they had one post of scouts set.
sentences.n: The same as the unit before; Čiqurqu-da is a place name with the dative-locative -da (Ming 地名 行).

sentences.t: Bidan-u maṅlan Altan, Qučar, Seṅgüm-tan Udkija kürčü baγ̇uja keġeldün büküi-dür

morph.gloss: we, us (inclusive: you and I) [咱的]
stem-final n before a case ending
forehead, brow; the vanguard (Ming 頭哨每 'lead scouts') [頭哨每]
Altan, a man's name (altan 'gold'; personal name) [人名]
Quchar, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
Sengüm, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
possessive plural: 'those with …, and the rest' (the back-vowel form -tan, though the stem is front-vowel; Shiratori's spelling) [等]
Udkija, a place name (Ming 地名) [地名]
converb: -ing (back-vowel form, as after a consonant)
to come down, dismount, camp [下咱]

sentences.l: Our vanguard Altan, Qučar, Seṅgüm-with Udkija arriving, let-us-camp saying-to-one-another, when-being,
sentences.i: When our vanguard — Altan, Quchar, Sengüm and the rest — reached Udkija and were saying to one another, "Let us make camp,"
sentences.n: Bidan-u is 'our' (bida 'we, inclusive', stem-n, genitive -u; Ming 咱的): the Ming's 咱 is the inclusive 'we', so 'our' takes in both allied vanguards (Altan and Quchar of Chinggis, Sengüm of Wang Qan). Seṅgüm-tan has -tan, 'and those with him' (人名 等). Udkija (地名) is a place. baγ̇uja (下咱) is baγ̇u- 'come down, camp' + the hortative -ja; keġeldün (相說) is keġe- 'say' with the reciprocal -ldü- and -n: 'saying to one another'. büküi-dür 'when being'.

sentences.t: Čiqurqu-da talbiγsan qaraγ̇ul-ača küġün qaγ̇ulžu irežü

words.reading: 赤中忽舌兒中忽-荅 Čiqurqu-da

morph.gloss: to let go, set loose, release [放了的]

sentences.l: At-Čiqurqu set-ones scouts-from man rushing coming,
sentences.i: a man from the scouts who had been posted at Chiqurqu, rushing and coming,
sentences.n: talbiγsan (放了的) is talbi- 'set' with the past participle -γsan, 'the ones set'; qaraγ̇ul-ača is 'from the scouts'; küġün 'man'. qaγ̇ulžu (奔着) 'rushing' and irežü (來着) 'coming' are two converbs before the finite verb in the next unit: 'rushing, coming, he came'.

sentences.t: dain aiši keġen kele kürgen irebe.

morph.gloss: to come (compare aisu-; stem uncertain) [來也]
to bring to, deliver (kür- 'reach' made causative; uncertain) [送]

sentences.l: Enemy is-coming saying, word bringing, came.
sentences.i: came crying "The enemy is coming!" and bringing the word.
sentences.n: dain is 'enemy' (敵) and aiši (來也) 'is coming', which I analyse as ai- 'come' + -ši, uncertain, resting on the Ming; keġen (麽道) ends the cry. kele kürgen irebe is 'bringing word, came': kürgen the converb -n. The cry has no quotation marks in Shiratori's text.

sentences.t: Tere kele ireġed ülü baγ̇un dain-u esergü kele abuja keġen

morph.gloss: that, that one; also 'he, she' (demonstrative and third-person pronoun) [那]
converb of completed action: having …ed (front-vowel form)

sentences.l: That word having-come, not camping, enemy's facing, word let-us-take saying,
sentences.i: When that word came, saying, "Let us not camp but go to meet the enemy and take word of them,"
sentences.n: tere kele ireġed is 'that word having come' (那 話 來了). ülü baγ̇un (不 下) is 'not coming down, not camping'. dain-u esergü is 'facing the enemy, against the enemy', the genitive before esergü as above. kele abuja (話 取咱) is 'let us take word' — get news, perhaps take someone to ask; ab- 'take' with the hortative -uja. The sense of the whole is uncertain, since the Ming glosses word by word.

sentences.t: jabužu kürülčežü kele abču ked bi keġen asaγasuγ̇asu

morph.gloss: to come together, meet (from kür- 'reach'; stem inferred from the Ming) [相接着]
converb: -ing (back-vowel form, as after a consonant)
who, which (plural; read from the Ming 誰每; uncertain) [誰每]

sentences.l: going, meeting-each-other, word taking, who-are (they) saying when-asking,
sentences.i: they went on and met them, and took their word; and when they asked, "Who are you?"
sentences.n: A converb chain, broken after asaγasuγ̇asu: jabužu 'going', kürülčežü 'coming together, meeting' (kür- 'reach' + a reciprocal ending, the stem inferred), abču 'taking'. ked bi keġen (誰每 有 麽道) is the question, 'who are they / who are you?'. ked I know only from the Ming 誰每, and its form is uncertain. asaγasuγ̇asu (問呵) is asaγa- 'ask' with a conditional ending the Ming glosses 呵 'if, when'; the extra -su- is unaccounted for.

morph.gloss: forehead, brow; the vanguard (Ming 頭哨 'lead scouts') [頭哨]
the Mongols, a people (the Ming writes 達達) [達達]

words.reading: 阿兀出-把阿禿舌兒 Aγ̇uču-Baγ̇atur

morph.gloss: A'uchu-Ba'atur, a man's name (baγ̇atur 'hero') [人名 勇士]

sentences.i: "Jamuqa's vanguard: from the Mongols, A'uchu-Ba'atur;
sentences.n: The answer is a list. Moṅγol-ača (達達處) is 'from the Mongols', but the Ming writes 達達, the Chinese word for the steppe peoples, so it is the Ming's name for the Mongols, not the Tatar of the text. Žamuqa-jin maṅlan is 'Jamuqa's vanguard'. Aγ̇uču-Baγ̇atur is a name given also, with the Taichi'ud, in §141.

sentences.t: Naiman-u Buiruγ-Qān Merkid-ün Toγtoγ̇a-Beki-jin köġün Qutu Oirad-un Quduγa-Beki

morph.gloss: Buiruq Qan, a man's name (personal name; Qān 'ruler') [人名]
genitive: of (front-vowel form, after a consonant) [的]
Toqto'a Beki, a man's name (one two-part name) [人名]
Qutu, a man's name (personal name) [(兒)名]
genitive: of (back-vowel form, after a consonant) [的]
Quduqa Beki, a man's name (personal name) [人名]

sentences.l: Naiman's Buiruγ-Qān; Merkid's Toγtoγ̇a-Beki's son Qutu; Oirad's Quduγa-Beki;
sentences.i: of the Naiman, Buiruq Qan; of the Merkid, Toqto'a Beki's son Qutu; of the Oirat, Quduqa Beki;
sentences.n: The list continues, each people in the genitive before its man: with the Mongols' Aγ̇uču-Baγ̇atur in the unit before, the four leaders named as Jamuqa's vanguard (cf. §141). Quduγa-Beki is printed with a γ here and Quduqa in §143.

morph.gloss: forehead, brow; the vanguard (Ming 頭哨 'lead scouts') [頭哨]

sentences.i: These four have marched as Jamuqa's vanguard."
sentences.n: ede dörben is 'these four', matching the four names. jabužuγ̇ui (行了有) is jabu- 'go' with the past -žuγ̇ui, 'went, have gone'; said in a report, I take it as 'have marched'.

sentences.t: Bidan-u maṅlan teden-dür uṅšilaldužu unšižu žilda boldažu

morph.gloss: we, us (inclusive: you and I) [咱的]
stem-final n before a case ending
forehead, brow; the vanguard (Ming 頭哨 'lead scouts') [頭哨]
that, that one; plural tede 'those' (here teden-) [他每]
to call out, shout (stem inferred from the Ming 呼) [共呼着]
late, evening (read from the Ming 晩) [晩]
to be made, become (passive; stem uncertain) [被做着]

sentences.l: Our vanguard to-them calling-together, calling, late being-made,
sentences.i: Our vanguard called out to them and they called back, evening coming on,
sentences.n: Bidan-u maṅlan is 'our vanguard'. teden-dür (他每行) is 'to them' — teden the plural 'those', with the dative-locative. uṅšilaldužu (共呼着) is 'calling together', with the reciprocal -ldu-, so 'calling to one another'; unšižu (喚着) 'calling'. žilda boldažu (晩 被做着) is 'late being made', 'it getting late'; bolda- is read from the Ming and is uncertain.

sentences.t: manaγar qadqulduja keġežü ičužu γol-dur neilen qonoba.

words.reading: 中合惕中忽勒都︀牙 qadqulduja

morph.gloss: to fight, strike (stem inferred from the Ming 殺) [厮殺︀咱]
to withdraw, draw back (stem inferred from the Ming 退) [退着]
centre, main body; the Ming here reads 大營 'main camp' (elsewhere 澗 'stream') [大營]
to join, to come together (Ming 相合) [相合]

sentences.l: Tomorrow let-us-fight saying, withdrawing, main-camp-at joining, spent-the-night.
sentences.i: "Let us fight tomorrow," they said; and drawing back, they joined up at the main camp and passed the night.
sentences.n: qadqulduja (厮殺咱) is 'let us fight one another': a stem qadqu- (the Ming 殺 'kill, fight'), the reciprocal -ldu- and the hortative -ja. ičužu (退着) 'withdrawing, drawing back'. γol-dur (大營 裏) puts γol, which the Ming reads here as the main camp (elsewhere 澗, a stream), with the dative-locative. neilen (相合) 'joining' and qonoba 'spent the night'. Who says 'let us fight tomorrow' — both sides, in the reciprocal — is not told.

morph.gloss: to come together, meet (from kür- 'reach'; stem inferred) [相接着]
Köiten, a place name (Ming 地名) [地名]

sentences.i: The next day they advanced and met, and drew up their battle-lines at Köiten;
sentences.n: manaγarši (明日) is manaγar 'tomorrow, next day' with -ši 'to, toward', the ending also in uruγši, doroγši, deġegši. jabuγ̇ulžu (行着) is 'advancing', jabu- with the causative -γ̇ul-; kürülčežü 'meeting' as in §142. Köiten is a place (Ming 地名) with no case ending; 'at' is the sense. baildužu (對陣着) is bai- 'stand' with the reciprocal -ldu-: 'standing against one another', 'taking up battle order'.

words.reading: 亦中忽舌里中合勒敦 iquriγaldun

morph.gloss: to bind together, link up (stem inferred from the Ming 相梆 'bind') [相梆]

words.reading: 只卜失額舌侖勒㕓 žibšiġerülčen

morph.gloss: to put in order, array (stem inferred from the Ming 整搠; uncertain) [共整搠]

sentences.i: while they were linking up and putting themselves in order, down the line and up it,
sentences.n: doroγši (往下) and deġegši (往上) are 'toward the lower' and 'toward the upper', with the same -ši; here, I suppose, the lower and upper ends of the line, but the Ming gives no more than 'down, up'. iquriγaldun (相梆) is 'binding together', from a stem iquriγa- that I take from the Ming; žibšiġerülčen (共整搠) is 'arraying together, putting in order'. Both are battle-order words, read from the Ming, and uncertain.

sentences.t: müd Buiruγ-Qān, Quduqa qojar žada modekün ažuγ̇ui.

morph.gloss: they (third-person plural; Ming 他每; the exact form is uncertain) [他每]
Buiruq Qan, a man's name (personal name; Qān 'ruler') [人名]
Quduqa, a man's name (personal name; the same Ming characters as Quduγa-Beki) [人名]
jada, the art of raising wind and rain (Ming 能致風雨的事) [能致風雨的事]
to know (printed modekün, with o; the stem is mede-) [知]

sentences.l: They, Buiruγ-Qān, Quduqa the-two jada knowing were.
sentences.i: Among them, Buiruq Qan and Quduqa, the two, knew the jada, the art of bringing wind and rain.
sentences.n: žada (the Ming's 能致風雨的事 'the matter that can bring wind and rain') is, from the Ming, the working of wind and rain; no more is told. müd is 'they' (Ming 他每; the form is uncertain). modekün (知) is mede- 'know' with the participle -kün, 'one who knows'. Quduqa has the same Ming characters as Quduγa-Beki (§141–142); Shiratori romanises the two differently, so it is the same man or a very close name.

morph.gloss: jada, the art of raising wind and rain
to become, to be; here the Ming 欲做 'wishing to do, about to' [欲做]
jada, the art of raising wind and rain (Ming 風雨) [風雨]
to turn over, upset (stem inferred from the Ming 翻) [翻着]

sentences.i: When they set about working the jada, and the jada turned,
sentences.n: Žadalaqun is žada + the verb-maker -la- 'make jada' + the participle -qun, which the Ming takes as a noun, 致風雨的事 'the doing of jada'. bolun (欲做) here means 'wanting to, about to', not the usual 'being'. hurbažu (翻着) is 'turning over, overturning', the stem hurba- from the Ming. The storm turns on those who raise it, which the next unit says outright.

morph.gloss: they (third-person plural; Ming 他每; the exact form is uncertain) [他每]
their (third-person genitive stem, back-vowel partner of in-; placed after its word) [(他的)]
jada, the art of raising wind and rain (Ming 風雨) [風雨]

sentences.i: the storm came upon them.
sentences.n: an-u deġere (他的 上) is 'upon them', an-u being the back-vowel partner of in-ü, the third-person genitive set after its word — here after the pronoun müd. žada bolžuγ̇u (風雨 做了) is 'the jada became, was made': the weather arose on them. The Ming 做了 'was made' leaves the cause open.

sentences.t: Müd jabun jadažu nuras-tur γuladu- γ̇ad"

morph.gloss: they (third-person plural; Ming 他每; the exact form is uncertain) [他每]
gully, ditch (stem read from the Ming 溝) [溝]
to fall, topple over (stem uncertain; the first half of γuladu-γ̇ad, split at the line end) [倒]
converb of completed action: having …ed (back-vowel form; the second half of γuladu-γ̇ad) [了]

sentences.i: Unable to go on, they fell into the gullies,
sentences.n: jabun jadažu (行 不能着) is 'going, being unable' — jabu- and jada-, 'not able to go'. nuras-tur (溝 裏) is 'in the gullies', a plural -s with the dative-locative -tur; the stem nura- is read from the Ming 溝. γuladu- and γ̇ad are one word, γuladu-γ̇ad (倒了, 'having fallen'), split by Shiratori's line-end hyphen; the stem is uncertain. A closing quotation mark follows γ̇ad with no opening mark anywhere before it, so the quotation (if there is one) is not clear.

sentences.t: teṅgeri-de ese taγ̇alaγdaba bida" keġeldüġed butaražuγ̇ui.

morph.gloss: Heaven, the sky as a power [天]
dative-locative: by, to (front-vowel form; names the doer of a passive) [行]
to love, favour (stem inferred from the Ming 愛) [被愛了]
converb of completed action: having …ed (front-vowel form)
to scatter, break up (stem inferred from the Ming 潰散) [潰散了]

sentences.l: By-Heaven not were-loved we" saying-together, scattered.
sentences.i: "Heaven has not favoured us," they said together, and they scattered.
sentences.n: teṅgeri-de (天 行) is 'by Heaven' — the dative-locative naming the doer of the passive, as with Žürkin-e in §136. ese (不曾) 'not yet, not' is the negative for past actions. taγ̇alaγdaba (被愛了) is 'was loved', taγ̇ala- (the Ming 愛) with the passive -γda- and the past -ba; 'favoured' is my reading of 'loved by Heaven'. bida is 'we'. keġeldüġed 'having said together'. butaražuγ̇ui (潰散了) is 'scattered, broke up', butara- from the Ming. A closing quotation mark follows bida, matching the one in the previous unit.
